newsitem.title: USA: S.F. stadium backers outspend project foes - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.F. stadium backers outspend project foes - paper.

text.p: Supporters of a proposed $537 million football stadium and retail complex in San Francisco have far outspent project foes, according to a published report on Friday.

The stadium backers have raised $838,000 and spent $700,000 as part of a campaign urging voters to support the project. The opponents have raised $50,000 and spent $48,000 in their bid to block the project, the San Francisco Chronicle newspaper reported.

The proposed stadium and retail project would cost an estimated $537 million, including $250 million to build a stadium for the National Football League's San Francisco 49ers and $200 million for the entertainment and shopping complex.
In February, the city's Board of Supervisors passed a resolution placing a bond measure on the ballot to help build the complex.
If approved by voters in June, the ballot proposition would authorize the city to issue lease-revenue bonds in a principal amount not exceeding $100 million.
